title: Phased Feedback-Loop Protocol & Observability Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a lightweight, repeatable protocol for cross-functional phased rollouts (pilot -> canary -> ramp -> steady) and A/B experiments for inference changes (model swaps, quantization, caching, routing). Focus: minimize customer impact, detect degradation in quality/perf/cost early, and close the feedback loop between product, SRE, engineers, and CS.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to changes that affect model behavior or inference runtime path (model versions, prompt templates, quantization, KV cache changes, batching policy, routing rules).
- Excludes purely client-side UI experiments (handled by frontend experimentation).
- Assumes instrumentation (traces, structured logs, sampling) is available for request->model mapping.

Rollout taxonomy (practical shorthand):
- Pilot (internal + friendly customers): low-risk validation, manual checks, not automated gating. Duration: 2–5 days.
- Canary (progressive user traffic): staged percentages (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 10%). Short observation windows between steps.
- Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 75% over multiple days with automated monitoring.
- Steady: full traffic; shift to normal monitoring cadence and post-mortem checklist.
- A/B experiment: randomized traffic split with explicit hypothesis, sample sizing, and statistical test plan.

Safety buckets and decision criteria (stoplight):
- Green: no action. All primary metrics within tolerance.
- Yellow: slow rollout, notify stakeholders, increase sample capture, run manual quality checks.
- Red: immediate rollback or divert traffic to fallback; open incident/ops ticket.

Suggested metric groups and example thresholds (starting point — tune per product):
1) Latency and reliability (engine/SRE):
  - p50/p95/p99 latency per route/model: alert if p95 increases > 2x baseline or absolute p99 > 2s for sync routes.
  - Error rate (5xx, timeouts): alert if rate increases by > 3x or > 0.5% absolute (whichever smaller).
2) Cost and throughput (infra/finops):
  - Cost-per-request or cost-per-token: follow a 20% deviation budget during canary; investigate >20% regression.
  - Throughput/backpressure signals: queue growth, OOM events.
3) Output quality (product/ML):
  - Eval-set drift: run nightly small eval of core prompt set; flag >5% drop in task-specific metric (F1, exact match, BLEU as appropriate).
  - Production signal proxies: user acceptance, downstream task failure rate, CTR or conversion where applicable.
  - Hallucination proxy: heuristic-based filters (e.g., nonsensical token patterns, out-of-domain markers); alert on >X events per 10k responses.
4) Privacy & safety (privacy/legal):
  - PII redaction failure rate: any increase >0% triggers hold and investigation.
  - Toxicity/safety triggers: automated classifiers should not spike.

Observation windows and sampling plan:
- Small canaries (<=1%): 30–60 minutes observation window, collect 1000+ samples if possible.
- Medium canaries (1–10%): 2–6 hours window.
- Large ramps (>10%): 24–48 hours per step.
- Sample capture: keep full request/response for 1% of traffic (rotating key-space sampling), store stripped samples for 7 days by default. Privacy: run PII redaction pipeline before retention.

Instrumentation checklist (REQ for a safe rollout):
- Routing tag: request.metadata.rollout_id and cohort / experiment_id attached to traces.
- Model provenance: model.id, model.commit/hash, quantization flag, kernel profile in logs.
- Token-level counters: input_tokens, generated_tokens, cache_hits.
- Error taxonomy: classify by error kind (timeout, OOM, model_error, validation_failure).
- Snapshotting: store 1 in N full responses for manual QA; store additional triggered samples when quality heuristics fire.
- Latency buckets and percentiles exposed per cohort: p50/p90/p95/p99.

Cohort selection heuristics and fairness notes:
- Prefer geographically and client-type diverse cohorts early. Avoid sending privacy-regulated customers (e.g., EU-regulated corp if not approved) to initial canaries unless explicit opt-in.
- Sticky routing: once a user is assigned a cohort for an A/B experiment or canary, they should remain for the duration of the experiment to reduce crossover noise.
- Avoid correlating cohort assignment with account tier or traffic pattern unless the hypothesis requires it. Document exceptions.

A/B experiment quick plan template (use for product experiments):
- Hypothesis: clear, measurable (e.g., "Model v2 reduces average completion tokens by 10% with same task success").
- Primary metric: single metric that decides success. Secondary metrics: latency, error rate, cost.
- Sample size estimate: back-of-envelope rules (detect 5–10% lift with >80% power -> need thousands to tens of thousands of users; consult analytics team).
- Randomization: server-side SDK, per-user consistent buckets.
- Analysis window: pre-specify duration and stopping criteria; do not peek repeatedly unless using sequential tests.
- Statistical test: t-test or permutation for continuous metrics, Fisher/Chi-sq for binary. Multiple comparisons: correct if testing >1 primary metric.

Automation and rollback policies:
- Automatic throttle: if infra alerts hit critical thresholds (p99 latency, error spike), system should divert traffic automatically to fallback model or previous stable route.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed: default to fail-open for non-safety features (redirect to baseline model). For safety-sensitive changes, fail-closed may be required.
- Post-rollback: require mandatory retrospective (owner + SRE + product) within 48 hours.

Cross-functional roles and responsibilities (minimal RACI):
- Product owner: defines hypothesis, primary metric, and acceptance criteria.
- Engineering owner: implements routing/config, verifies instrumentation, executes rollout.
- SRE: defines infra-based thresholds, implements auto-divert, monitors system-level telemetry.
- Applied ML: defines eval-set and offline regressions, conducts manual quality review for flagged samples.
- Customer Success / Support: watches user reports, surfaces customer-impacting issues.
- Legal/Privacy: sign-off if data retention or PII handling changes.

Manual QA checklist (for each canary step):
- Run 20 curated prompts through both baseline and candidate; compare outputs and flag regressions.
- Sanity check 50 randomly sampled production responses for obvious failures.
- Confirm no PII leakage in sample retention.

Open engineering TODOs (short lived):
- [ ] Add consistent rollout_id to trace headers (ENG-2201).
- [ ] Implement sample-store with redaction pipeline and 7-day TTL (ENG-2233).
- [ ] Add configurable cost-per-token alerting to infra monitoring (SRE-117).

Operational playbook (quick run):
1) Preflight: author hypothesis doc, attach to rollout config, run offline eval, get privacy/legal signoff if required.
2) Pilot: internal validation for 48–72h.
3) Canary: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% with observation windows and manual QA.
4) Ramp: 25%/50%/75% with 24h windows.
5) Steady and iterate: monitor weekly, schedule post-launch quality sweep at 7 days.

Postmortem template (if rollback or bad signal):
- Timeline of events, root cause hypothesis, mitigation taken, monitoring gaps, action items with owners and due dates.

Notes and unresolved questions (for product discussion):
- How aggressive should cost regression gates be for optimizations that give long-term savings but short-term latency spike?
- Should we maintain a separate "high-sensitivity" rollout path for enterprise customers with stricter observation windows?
- How to incorporate human-in-the-loop labeling quickly during canary to accelerate quality signal?

Appendix: quick checklist for small feature owners (one-pager you can paste into PR):
- Add rollout_id to request.
- Define primary metric and acceptance thresholds.
- Ensure sampling/retention and redaction configured.
- Add automated alerts for p95/p99 latency and error rate.
- Schedule manual QA session between canary steps.

(End of working draft)

Author notes: this is intentionally practice-focused and pragmatic. Will iterate with SRE and Applied ML on numeric thresholds after two pilot runs.
